A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, complete 37-page versions of the same work. The main text, equations, five figures, references, and Appendices A–L support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original convergence simulations and semi-synthetic credit-scoring and rideshare experiments, including Figures 2–5 and Appendices I–J.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulation and experimental outcomes, including the credit-scoring and rideshare results in the appendices.

M1.justification: The ARM historical-distribution aggregation procedure, optimization objectives, and proximal variants are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic lower-bound example, Give Me Some Credit classification task, and Boston Uber/Lyft pricing game.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: aggregation windows 1–5 in Figure 2 and 1, 2, 4, t/2, and all snapshots in the credit-scoring and rideshare comparisons. Window 1 remains standard RRM.

E3.justification: The loss-shift and performative-risk metrics and experimental settings are retained, including 50 credit-scoring iterations and 25 demand samples with up to 40 retraining steps in the rideshare experiment.

E4.justification: The same aggregation-window analyses, synthetic lower-bound validation, and supplementary risk trajectories appear in Figures 2–5. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 500-run credit-scoring averages and 200-run rideshare averages. The initialization and randomization description in Appendix I and the figures' uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 2–5 retain identical plotted content and numerical annotations. The reported convergence trends, window comparisons, and qualitative findings also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The assumptions, Theorems 1–9, auxiliary lemmas, and appendix proofs are unchanged, including the proximal results in Appendices F.1 and K. Mathematical spacing changes do not alter the formulas.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about historical-data aggregation, broader stability conditions, improved upper bounds, tightness, and ARM lower bounds.

C2.justification: The discussions of diminishing returns, resource costs, and transient performative risk are unchanged. Appendix L retains the qualifications about stability versus convergence speed and deterministic access to full distributions.

D1.justification: Appendices I–J retain the same hyperparameters, optimizer, hardware, runtime, sampling, and initialization details. Dataset access links are unchanged; the settings accompanying Equation 53 merely move to page 34.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, and the positioning relative to Perdomo et al. and Mofakhami et al. are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 replaces 'Preprint. Under review.' with the NeurIPS 2025 conference identification and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Research prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 5 changes from two side-by-side panels to vertically stacked panels, moving Equation 53 and part of Appendix J's discussion onto page 34. The plotted content and caption are retained; other typesetting differences are limited.

improvement.justification: v3 updates publication metadata and rearranges Figure 5 while preserving the methods, theory, empirical evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations. These limited presentation changes leave overall clarity and scientific support essentially unchanged.
